title: Navbar
summary: A navbar groups the main site links. On a small screen, its links can fit inside a menu that opens and closes.
introduction: A navbar groups the main site links. On a small screen, its links can fit inside a menu that opens and closes. Start with a few clear links. Then connect a menu button to the correct menu id and load the Bootstrap JavaScript it needs.
learningObjectives: Assemble the navbar markup: brand, toggler, collapse wrapper and nav links
Choose the breakpoint at which the navbar expands with navbar-expand-*
Mark the current page and add a dropdown and a search form
Switch to a dark navbar and fix it to the top of the page

blocks.text: A navbar is a `<nav class="navbar">` containing a container, which gives it side padding, and inside that three things: the **brand** (a link with the site name), the **toggler** (a hamburger button shown only on small screens) and the **collapse wrapper** that holds the links. The toggler and the wrapper are connected by an id: the button's `data-bs-target` must name the wrapper, and that connection is what the JavaScript bundle uses to open and close the menu.

blocks.title: A complete responsive navbar
blocks.code:
Garden Club
  • Home
  • Events
  • Join

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
992px and wider: a light grey bar with "Garden Club" on the left and Home, Events, Join on the same line; Home is dark (current page), the others are grey
Below 992px: the bar shows "Garden Club" and a bordered hamburger button on the right; the links are hidden
Clicking the hamburger (JavaScript bundle required) slides the three links open, stacked under the brand; clicking again closes them

rows: The flex container that lays the parts out in a row with `.5rem` vertical padding
Below the lg breakpoint the links collapse behind the toggler; from 992px they display inline
A background that follows the colour mode: light grey in light mode, dark grey in dark mode
Larger (1.25rem) text for the site name, usually a link to the home page
The hamburger button and the three-line icon inside it
Tell the bundle which element the button opens; `aria-controls` repeats the id for assistive technology
The wrapper that is hidden on small screens until toggled
The list, items and links, styled without bullets and with hover and active colours
Mark the link for the page the user is on, visually and for screen readers

blocks.text: `navbar-expand-{sm|md|lg|xl|xxl}` sets the width from which the links show inline. Pick it by measuring: with three short links, `md` is enough; with six links, a dropdown and a search form, the row will not fit until `lg` or `xl`. Plain `navbar-expand` keeps the bar horizontal at every size, and leaving the class out keeps it collapsed at every size, which suits a mobile-style menu even on desktops.

A dropdown is a `nav-item` with the extra class `dropdown`, a link marked `dropdown-toggle` with `data-bs-toggle="dropdown"`, and a `dropdown-menu` list. Popper, included in the bundle, positions the menu. A form can sit directly in the collapse wrapper; `me-auto` on the link list pushes everything after it to the right edge.

blocks.title: Replace the collapse wrapper from the first example with this
blocks.code:
• Home
  • Events
    • Talks
    • Garden visits
    • Past events

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
992px and wider: Home and "Events" with a small down-pointing triangle on the left; the search field and green outlined button sit at the right edge
Clicking Events opens a white panel beneath it listing Talks, Garden visits, a thin divider line, Past events; clicking anywhere else closes it
Below 992px with the menu open: the links are stacked, then the search form below them with an 8px gap

blocks.text: Before 5.3 you coloured a navbar with `navbar-dark` and `bg-dark`. In 5.3 `navbar-dark` is deprecated: set `data-bs-theme="dark"` on the `<nav>` instead, which flips the brand, link and toggler colours to light, and pick any dark background utility. `fixed-top` pins the bar to the viewport so it stays visible while scrolling; `sticky-top` lets it scroll with the page until it reaches the top, then sticks.

blocks.title: A dark navbar fixed to the top
blocks.code:
Garden Club
  • Events
  • Join

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
A #212529 bar pinned to the top of the window; "Garden Club" in white, the links in light grey turning white on hover
The page scrolls underneath the bar; without extra top padding on the body, the first 56px of content start hidden behind it

blocks.text: A fixed navbar is taken out of the page flow, so add `padding-top` to the `<body>` equal to the bar's height (about 56px with the defaults) or the top of your content disappears behind it. `sticky-top` does not have this problem.

blocks.title: Common mistake: the toggler does nothing
blocks.text: Nine times out of ten the hamburger is wired to the wrong id. `data-bs-target="#mainNav"` must match `id="mainNav"` on the collapse wrapper exactly, including case, and the `#` belongs only in the target. The other causes, in order: the JavaScript bundle is not loaded, the attribute is spelled the Bootstrap 4 way (`data-toggle`), or the wrapper is missing the `collapse` class, in which case the links are always visible and the button has nothing to show.

blocks.title: One navbar per page
blocks.text: Keep a single `<nav>` for the main navigation and give it an `aria-label` (for example `aria-label="Main"`) if the page has other navigation such as a footer menu, so screen reader users can tell them apart.

questions.question: With `navbar-expand-md`, on which screens are the links hidden behind the toggler?
questions.explanation: The expand class names the width from which links display inline. md starts at 768px, so narrower viewports see the collapsed menu.

questions.question: Besides the `active` class, the current page's link should carry the attribute `___="page"` so screen readers announce it.
questions.explanation: aria-current="page" is the accessible counterpart of the visual .active class; Bootstrap's CSS does not add it for you.

seo.title: Bootstrap Navbar – Responsive Navigation with Toggler
seo.description: Build a responsive Bootstrap 5.3 navbar with a brand, links, dropdown and search form, choose the expand breakpoint, mark the current page and switch it to dark.
